ratings_why.fun: Three engines that feed each other (strikes, Hoards, counts), and every slot is a unit-or-Light decision every turn; a few flat cards keep it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because empty slots become the resource: no tribe today plays on the slots it leaves empty, with defence, savings and cash-in all on the same lamp.

verdict_why: The engines lock together well now; what is left is a rules line and some tuning, and another full pass would mostly make it different.

points.text: Say whether a Light covered by a unit summoned mid-fight still counts as lit (for Tiddy Mun's redirect and Map-Seller's 'not struck'). Aarnivalkea answers this for its Wisps, but the Snuff keyword doesn't.

Follette's front Lights are fight-only, so Joan's Bury on them flows to your nearest lasting Light: a front-row funnel into a back-row bank. Worth calling out in the Hoard Mere build, as it's the best hidden combo here.
Old Will counts Follette's Lights only if Follette comes first in reading order. That's a nice positioning puzzle; show the count live in the recruit preview so players find it.
Selling Little Phos lights its slot, which a Spunkie or any unit can then snuff for Stingy Jack gold. A card that pays a tiny bit for selling Wisps onto Lights would make that cycle a real line.
Map-Seller only counts Lights; letting it also pay when a Light is snuffed would tie it into the snuff engine instead of sitting beside it.

standouts.why: Risen Wisps fight, die, relight the lamp, which then gets struck and grows under Joan: a loop across three subsystems that stays linear.
Swapping with a back-row Light pulls the Light forward and tucks the carry away; a one-card trick with many uses.
Hops across Hoards each turn and leaves a fresh lamp behind; with Turncoat and Stingy Jack it turns tidying the board into an engine.

weakest.why: Flat gold for unstruck back Lights; works, but asks nothing of you.
A plain 'grow when X happens' seed with a cap; no twist on the Light idea.
Lights one slot a turn with no choice of where; the slot rule decides for you.

flags.note: With Tiddy Mun each Light is struck twice, so one big enemy carry can hit its own board twice for its full Attack.
Golden Tiddy Mun with golden Barn Owl stacks to several times Tier 5's in-fight target, as the design itself notes.
Bury +2/+2 under each of 4 early Lights is about 16 stats at Tier 2, double the 'once' target, though locked until snuffed.
